shadows.name: ambient
shadows.purpose: Default resting elevation for every card, rung, callout, day block. Ambient and always-on, not a hover response.

shadows.name: lifted

motion.name: rung-in
motion.purpose: Ladder rungs slide up and fade in on load, in sequence — the sequence itself is information (rung order). Smooth exponential ease-out, no overshoot/bounce (replaced the earlier springy easing as a deliberate AI-tell purge).

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: Interactive card hover: translateY(-2px) plus shadow deepen (ambient → lifted).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) disables all animation/transition and forces scroll-behavior: auto

narrative.overview:
This is a guide written by and for people who now live partly in a terminal. The visual system fuses two things the product itself is about: a command-line identity (the ❯ brand glyph, literal monospace command syntax, a mini terminal window in the hero) and the three-rung ladder — Prompt → Skill → Subagent — the whole guide teaches. The tier ramp isn't decorative color variety; it's the one idea made visible, so the deepening violet-to-indigo progression (--t1 → --t2 → --t3) must always track that specific meaning wherever it appears, never be reused as generic accent color.

The feel is precise and unshowy: warm, slightly desaturated paper (never bright white, deliberately not cream — "#F4F1EA reads as AI-default" per the token file's own comment) carries small, confident type moves rather than large decorative gestures. Cards and rungs sit gently, permanently lifted off the paper — elevation here is ambient and material, not a state you earn by hovering.

A second pass removed a set of recognizable AI-generated-UI tells that had crept into the shipped build despite the direction above: a decorative hairline grid behind every hero, a colored border-left/border-top accent on rungs/callouts/day-blocks/compare-panels, a kicker/eyebrow label above every hero h1, and springy overshoot easing on the rung entrance animation. Category and tier meaning now live in badges, tinted backgrounds, and colored headings instead of border accents; heroes lead directly with their h1 at a larger, more confident scale; motion decelerates smoothly instead of bouncing.

Confirmed rejection: this system explicitly does not chase generic "AI-product" visual habits — no glossy gradient hero, no purple-on-white SaaS default, no stock illustration, no kicker-plus-headline template, no colored side-accent cards, no bounce easing. Where purple/violet appears, it is load-bearing (the ladder), not a category costume.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, matte paper surfaces (never pure white, never cream) with a bright off-white card surface for content
A deepening violet→indigo tier ramp that always means Prompt→Skill→Subagent, carried by badges and tinted backgrounds — never a border accent, never a generic accent
Terminal/CLI vocabulary throughout: the ❯ glyph, monospace command chips, a dark terminal window
Ambient, always-on soft shadows — material lift at rest, not a hover reward
Small radii (5–20px), thin uniform 1px rules on every edge — no accent borders anywhere
Every hero h1 leads its page directly, no kicker or eyebrow above it
Motion decelerates smoothly (exponential ease-out); nothing overshoots or springs

rules.name: The Ladder-Only Rule
rules.body: The three tier colors (Prompt Violet, Skill Violet, Subagent Indigo) and their soft/line tints exist to encode which rung of Prompt → Skill → Subagent a piece of UI refers to. Never repurpose them as a generic fourth or fifth accent color.

rules.name: The Soft/Line Rule
rules.body: Every accent color ships as a triplet: solid for icons/text/fills, -soft for background wash, -line for border. Never place a solid accent directly on Paper without its matching tints doing the transition.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Chrome Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for structural/interface text — never for headlines or body prose. If something is set in mono, it is labeling or instructing, not narrating.

rules.name: The Always-Lifted Rule
rules.body: Cards and rungs are never flat at rest. If a new component needs to feel calmer than the default card, reduce padding or remove the border — don't remove the shadow.

rules.name: The Badge-Not-Border Rule
rules.body: Category and tier meaning live in a colored number badge, a tinted background, or a colored heading — never in a border accent. A colored border-left or border-top on a card, rung, callout, day block, or compare panel is a rejected pattern here.

dos: Do keep the tier ramp (Prompt Violet / Skill Violet / Subagent Indigo) meaning-locked to the three rungs; never introduce a fourth 'tier-like' color.
Do pair every accent color with its own -soft background and -line border tint rather than placing a solid accent directly on Paper.
Do set structural/interface text (nav, tags, code, terminal, callout/card labels) in JetBrains Mono, uppercase, widely tracked where it's a label.
Do give every card-like surface an ambient shadow at rest (11px radius, 1px Rule border) — nothing floats with zero elevation.
Do carry category/tier meaning with a colored number badge, a tinted background, or a colored heading — never a border accent.
Do let every hero h1 lead the page directly, with the lede paragraph doing any framing a label might otherwise carry.
donts: Don't use a bright/pure white or cream background — Paper is deliberately warm and slightly desaturated.
Don't reach for a generic purple-on-white 'AI SaaS' gradient hero, glossy CTA, or stock illustration — the violet in this system is load-bearing ladder meaning, not category decoration.
Don't make elevation hover-only. Shadows here are ambient/material; hover deepens an existing shadow, it doesn't create one from flat.
Don't set headline or body prose in JetBrains Mono — mono means interface chrome, not narration.
Don't hand-roll a new border-radius value outside 5px / 11px / 20px (or 999px for fully round pills/chips).
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above an h1/h2 headline — removed sitewide as a recognizable AI-generated-UI tell; the headline carries its own weight.
Don't add a colored border-left/border-top accent to a card, rung, callout, day block, or compare panel — removed sitewide; use a badge, a tinted background, or a colored heading instead.
Don't draw a decorative hairline grid or line-field behind a hero — removed; trust the type and the terminal demo to carry the hero.
Don't use overshoot/bounce easing — replaced sitewide with a smooth exponential ease-out (cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)).
Don't use Ink, Faint (--ink-3) for real reader-facing text on the actual guide pages — it fails WCAG AA; it's reserved for the showcase.html demo product's own palette.
